verdict.rationale: Modal's Python SDK lets code programmatically deploy and interact with the platform, including requesting specific GPU types via the `gpu` argument, and it ships an official CLI plus an agent skill, so an agent can provision GPUs and run workloads without the console. Monitoring and teardown are less clearly agent-addressable: logs and metrics are claimed, and containers spin down automatically, but the evidence shows no programmatic metrics or log API and no explicit stop or teardown command. Missing for 10: documented programmatic monitoring endpoints, an explicit teardown or stop API/CLI command, an official MCP server, and independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end agent run.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
Modal distributes an [official skill](./py/modal/skills/modal/SKILL.md) to help coding agents use its latest features.
Comprehensive logs and metrics for every function and sandbox, down to the container.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
